what_it_does: An Image Signal Processor (ISP) is the chip inside a camera or self-driving car that turns raw sensor data into a clean, usable image. ISPs have many adjustable settings (called hyperparameters) — things like how aggressively to reduce noise or how to correct color — that must be tuned differently for bright sun versus rain or night. Tuning these by hand is impractical at runtime, and pre-computed offline settings cannot react to sudden environmental changes. MAS-ISP uses a team of reinforcement-learning agents (software programs that learn by trial and reward, like training a dog with treats) that cooperate in a master-slave arrangement to tune the ISP settings in real time while the camera is running. The paper also introduces new hardware tricks — a 'strip convolution' pattern and a dual-buffer memory design — that shrink the chip area needed for the on-device AI, making the whole system feasible on a real-time chip.
